question: Which of the following educational institute was established by Raja Ram Mohan Roy with the cooperation of David Hare in 1817 in Calcutta?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindu College**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hindu College was established in **1817 in Calcutta (now Kolkata)** by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in collaboration with David Hare.
 
• The institution was founded with the purpose of **promoting Western education** among the youth of Bengal.
 
• It is considered one of the oldest modern educational institutions in India and played a pivotal role in the **Bengal Renaissance**.
 
• Hindu College later evolved into the **Presidency College** in 1855 and subsequently became Presidency University in 2010.
 
• The college was instrumental in fostering a spirit of reform and awakening during the colonial period, influencing the rise of modern Indian nationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**

 
 
• Known as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance**, Raja Ram Mohan Roy was a prominent social reformer and educationist.
 
• He advocated for the abolition of practices like **Sati** and child marriage, and championed women's rights.
 
• He was also a supporter of modern education and played a major role in introducing English and Western learning in India.
 
 
 
• **David Hare**
 
 
• David Hare was a Scottish philanthropist and educator who dedicated his life to the cause of education in India.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing several educational institutions in Calcutta, including Hindu College and the Hare School.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Renaissance**
 
 
• The Bengal Renaissance was a cultural, social, and intellectual movement in Bengal during the 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• Key figures included Raja Ram Mohan Roy, Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, and Swami Vivekananda, among others.
 
• The movement aimed at reforming traditional practices and embracing modernity while preserving Indian cultural values.
 
 
 
• **Presidency University**
 
 
• Originally established as Hindu College, it became Presidency College in 1855 under the British colonial administration.
 
• It was granted the status of a university in 2010, marking its transformation into a premier institution for higher education and research in India.
